# Making a moving-house checklist quickly with any AI assistant

**Hook:** By the end of this guide, you'll have a personalised, week-by-week moving checklist you can actually use — no more lying awake wondering if you forgot something important. This is for anyone facing a house move who wants a calm, organised plan without spending an entire weekend researching what to do and when.

## Before you start

- An AI assistant you can chat with — **ChatGPT, Gemini, Claude, Microsoft Copilot, Le Chat** or **DeepSeek** all work fine. A free account is enough.
- A phone, tablet or computer with internet access.
- About 10–15 minutes of quiet time. The more honest detail you give the AI upfront, the better your list will be.

## Step 1 — Open a fresh chat with your AI assistant

Open whichever AI assistant you've chosen and start a brand-new conversation. A fresh chat matters because the AI works best when it's not mixing up your moving plans with an old conversation about recipes or work emails. Look for a button labelled **New chat**, **New conversation** or a simple **+** icon — it usually lives in the top-left corner or in a sidebar menu. Tap or click it, and a blank message box will appear. If you can't find that exact wording, look for a pencil icon, a **Compose** button, or just close any existing chat and open a new one.

💬 Example: nothing to type yet — just confirm the box is empty and ready.

You'll know it worked when the screen shows an empty text field with no previous questions or answers above it.

## Step 2 — Describe your move in plain words

In the empty box, write a short message explaining your situation. Think of it like briefing a helpful friend who's never met you. Include the rough date, where you're moving from and to (a suburb is fine), the size of the place, and who's coming with you — partner, kids, pets. Don't stress about being perfect; a few sentences are plenty. The AI uses this context to tailor the checklist, and the more honest you are about what's tricky (kids, fragile items, a long-distance move), the smarter its suggestions will be.

💬 Example: "I'm moving from a two-bedroom unit in Parramatta to a three-bedroom house in Newcastle around mid-October. It's me, my partner, and one cat. We've never done a big move before, so please don't assume we know the basics."

You'll know it worked when the AI replies by acknowledging your details or asking a sensible follow-up question.

## Step 3 — Ask for a week-by-week checklist

Now ask the AI to build the actual checklist, organised by how far out each task is. Most moving guides suggest starting around **8 weeks before** and ramping up the week of the move, so a structure like "8 weeks out, 4 weeks out, 2 weeks out, 1 week out, moving day, first week after" works beautifully. The more specific you are about the format, the less editing you'll do later. If you want the list as a table, a bullet list, or grouped by room, just say so — the AI will reshape it on the spot.

💬 Example: "Please make me a moving checklist organised by week: 8 weeks before, 4 weeks before, 2 weeks before, 1 week before, moving day, and the first week after. Use bullet points, and include things like address changes, utilities, packing, and looking after my cat during the move."

You'll know it worked when the AI replies with a structured list grouped under clear weekly headings.

## Step 4 — Add the things only you would know

Read through the list and you'll spot gaps — the school pickup, the plants on the balcony, the spare key with your neighbour, the gym membership. Tell the AI these in a follow-up message and ask it to slot them into the right week. This is where the checklist becomes genuinely yours rather than a generic download. It's also worth mentioning any deadlines you already know about: a lease end date, a kids' school start date, a removalist booking you've already made.

💬 Example: "Good start. Can you also add: my daughter starts Year 3 at Newcastle Public on 28 October so I need to enrol her by mid-September; I need to give my landlord 30 days' notice; and please add a reminder to drain the washing machine and defrost the freezer the day before."

You'll know it worked when the revised checklist includes your additions in the correct week, not dumped at the bottom.

## Step 5 — Save it somewhere you'll actually open

A checklist only helps if it's in front of you on the day. Ask the AI to give you the final list in a format that travels well — plain text you can copy, a table you can paste into a notes app, or a simple markdown version. Then copy it into **Notes**, **Google Keep**, **Apple Notes** or whatever app you already use every day. Some people prefer to print it and tick items off with a pen; others like a shared note their partner can edit. There's no right answer — pick what you'll actually use.

💬 Example: "Can you give me the final list as plain text I can paste into my notes app? Also, please put a star next to anything that's time-sensitive or easy to forget, like redirecting my mail at the post office."

You'll know it worked when you can paste the list into a notes app and read it without scrolling back to the chat.

## Step 6 — Use the AI for the tricky little jobs

The checklist is the main event, but the same chat can help with smaller moving headaches — drafting a notice to your landlord, writing a "what's in this box" labelling system, or planning what to pack in an overnight bag for moving day. Just ask in the same chat so the context stays alive. One honest note: the AI can draft messages and suggest ideas, but it **cannot** book removalists, update your address with the post office, or transfer your utilities — those are things only you (or a real person on the phone) can do.

💬 Example: "While you're at it, can you write a short, polite message to my landlord giving 30 days' notice? I'll fill in the dates and send it myself."

You'll know it worked when you have a draft you can copy, tweak, and send in under a minute.

## Common mistakes

- **Giving too little context.** A prompt like "make me a moving checklist" works, but the result will be generic. Add your dates, location, household and any quirks — the AI genuinely uses them.
- **Trying to fix everything in one giant prompt.** Smaller, conversational prompts ("here's my situation, now add these items, now format it differently") usually produce a far better final list than one enormous paragraph.
- **Forgetting to save the list.** Chats can vanish if you clear your history or switch devices. The moment you have a version you like, copy it into a notes app, email it to yourself, or screenshot it.
- **Assuming the AI knows your local rules.** Notice periods, bond rules and mail redirection rules vary by state and tenancy type. Treat the AI's suggestions as a starting point, then double-check anything legal or financial with the relevant authority.

## What this means for you

- **In everyday life:** Moving is one of life's most forgettable-yet-stressful events. A good checklist turns "did I remember everything?" into a calm "tick, tick, tick" — and an AI assistant can build one tailored to you in minutes, not hours.
- **For your business or work:** If you run a small business from home, a studio, or a shop, the same approach works for relocating your work setup — just swap in business-specific items like stock, signage, insurance and customer notifications.
- **If you're just getting started:** Don't overthink the prompt. Open any AI assistant, type what we did in Step 2, and let the conversation build from there. You can always refine it on the second pass.

## Try it now

Open any AI assistant you already use — on your phone or computer — and send this exact message: *"I'm moving house in about two months. Can you ask me a few questions so you can build me a week-by-week checklist that fits my situation?"* Answer the questions honestly, and you'll have a useful first draft before your coffee gets cold.
